reasons: Cited text supports the compliant claim: 24.1 grants Customer a consent-free assignment right to an Affiliate (defined at 1.1) or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, subject only to notice and assumption.
24.2 restricts Vendor asymmetrically (consent required, including transfer by change of control, with a never-to-a-competitor bar), matching the preferred position.

24.4 expressly negates any Vendor termination, suspension, repricing, fee acceleration or service reduction right on Customer's change of control, removing the walk-away risk; 24.3 is residual ('For other assignments') and uses the favourable consent standard, so it does not undercut 24.1.
13.3 aligns the licence transfer with permitted Section 24 assignments, so no lapse on assignment.
No redline or comment is expected for a compliant finding, and none was proposed; deterministic check confirms the successor/affiliate carve-out is present.
